content: HighWire Press is a division of the Stanford University Libraries that specializes in producing online versions of high-impact, peer-reviewed journals and other scholarly content. It has been recognized for its contributions to not-for-profit publishing, receiving the 2003 Association for Learned and Professional Society Publishers (ALPSP) Award for Service to Not-for-Profit Publishing. HighWire collaborates with scholarly societies, university presses, and publishers to host an extensive collection of clinical and research literature. Notably, more than 70 of the 200 most frequently cited scientific journals are hosted on HighWire. As a division of Stanford University Libraries, HighWire Press maintains the largest repository of high-impact, peer-reviewed content. This includes over 1,100 journals and more than 4 million full-text articles from over 130 scholarly publishers. Additionally, 5 million articles are available for free access. HighWire's journey began in 1995 when the Journal of Biological Chemistry (JBC) became available online through its platform. Since then, numerous prestigious journals, such as Science, The New England Journal of Medicine, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, and JAMA, have joined the service. In 2005, the HighWire website underwent a redesign, which received positive feedback in professional reviews. A notable feature introduced was the citation map, which allows researchers to trace a paper's citations across other articles and journals. Although HighWire primarily functions as a hosting platform, a 2007 study demonstrated that its search engine outperformed PubMed in identifying desired articles and provided a greater number of search results for the same queries. However, PubMed was found to be faster in terms of search speed.
